28.0.0.en: A short time after the preceding events, the Philistines decided to wage war against the people of the children of Israel, so they gathered all their armies to prepare for this war. Among the preparations made by "Achish," king of Gath, was that he spoke with David to secure his going out with him in the fight against Israel. This shows the measure of Achish's confidence in David, that he would ally himself with him against his own people, so much so that Achish's words did not take the form of a question but of a command.

28.1.0.en: Of course the situation was hard for David, and so he answered with wisdom and with an open-ended answer. He said to Achish, "You shall know what your servant can do," and he did not specify what he would do, but Achish understood from David's answer what he wanted to understand, namely David's agreement and allegiance to him. So Achish replied to his words that he trusted him with great trust, so much that he entrusted his life to him and would make him his personal guard.

28.1.1.en: When circumstances put you in a position to lie, do not rush, but ask God's help, and He will give you wisdom and you will give an answer that has no lie in it, and it will rescue you from the awkward situation. Only be careful to keep God before your eyes, so that you fear Him and hold fast to His commandments and seek His help, and He will never leave you and will always give you wisdom. The First Book of Samuel

28.2.s.en: (2) Saul asks the Lord about the war

28.2.1.en: Those with familiar spirits: the sorcerers who make use of demons in their evil works.

28.2.2.en: Wizards: those whom demons accompany and follow in their lives, so that they perform wonders and tell them hidden things.

28.2.3.en: This verse is a parenthesis in the events, but it is an introduction to what Saul would do afterward. It tells us of the death of Samuel the prophet, who represented the voice of God, and points to his exalted standing in all Israel's mourning for him and his burial with honor in his city, where he had lived all his life. As an introduction also to what is coming, we learn that Saul in the days of his early reign had put away those who had familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the soothsayers from all his kingdom, in keeping with God's Law (Deut 18:10, 11).

28.3.0.en: Shunem: it is the present town of Sulam, and it lies 3.5 miles north of Jezreel in the land of Issachar. Gilboa: it is now the village of Jilbun, and it lies in the Gilboa mountain range, which forms the northeastern part of the mountains of Ephraim, near the Jordan, opposite Shunem.

28.3.1.en: The two armies gathered in two positions with a plain between them, the valley of Jezreel. The Philistines were north of this valley, while the Israelites were south of it.

28.4.0.en: Because of the great numbers in the Philistine army, Saul was greatly afraid and went to inquire of God. But he had killed all the priests at "Nob," and none of them escaped except "Abiathar," who fled to David and carried with him the ephod and the stones of the Urim and Thummim. For this reason Saul received no answer from God in any form: not by dreams, nor by Urim and Thummim, since these were with Abiathar, nor by prophets, since he no longer had a prophet with him. And Saul's turning to God was out of fear of the Philistines, and not out of piety or faith in God.

28.4.1.en: Do not cut off the means that lead you to God, which are prayer, the Holy Bible, your relationship with the Church, and the sacraments, lest tribulation come upon you and you find no accustomed means that bring you to God, and you fall into bewilderment and trembling.

28.5.0.en: A woman that hath a familiar spirit: a soothsayer who consults demons and makes people think they are the spirits of the dead.

28.5.1.en: The First Book of Samuel. Endor: one of the cities of the tribe of Manasseh, lying about 9.5 km southeast of Nazareth.

28.5.2.en: Despair and distress took hold of Saul's soul when God did not answer him, and instead of repentance and remorse he turned to a greater error. He commanded his men to seek out for him any woman who practiced sorcery and was known to have contact with demons, so that he might go to her and ask her about the war. And his servants pointed him to a woman who practiced sorcery and divination and lived at Endor.

28.6.0.en: Bring up: because evil and righteous spirits were in Hades in the Old Testament, but the former in torment and the latter in rest, awaiting Christ's redemption to raise them to Paradise. Saul took two men of his followers and went with them to the woman by night so that no one would see him, and he disguised himself to hide his identity, and he asked two things of her: first, that she tell him the future by means of the familiar spirit, and then that she bring up for him the spirit of the person he would name to her.

28.6.1.en: God may delay His answer to your petition because of His divine wisdom, or His voice may not be clear to you in something you ask of Him. So beware of the helpers of Satan, and do not deal with an astrologer, a sorcerer, or a fortune-teller, even as a jest or for amusement, for by doing so you despise God Himself and hand yourself over as an easy prey to the enemy of good.

28.7.0.en: The woman answered Saul that everyone knew what Saul had done, gathering and killing every sorcerer and soothsayer in the kingdom. "Is this a trap and a test for me, so that you may destroy me?"

28.8.0.en: Saul swore to her by the name of the Lord to reassure her and gain his purpose, and when she asked him whom he wanted her to bring up, he told her that he wanted the spirit of Samuel the prophet so that he might speak with him. In Saul's oath there is an appearance of religion, but his heart was far from God, for how could he swear by God that no harm would come to her, when what he was doing was against God's Law, which commands the stoning of sorceresses (Lev 20:27)?

28.9.0.en: The woman was expecting one of the demons with whom she was accustomed to deal to appear, but Samuel's appearing with the splendor of the saints' appearance terrified her greatly, so that she cried out from the severity of the shock and surprise. And she learned from Samuel's spirit that the one speaking with her was King Saul himself, and in alarm she asked him why he had deceived her. Samuel's appearance was by God's permission and not by the power of divination, as a final warning to Saul, that perhaps he might repent.

28.9.1.en: From this it appears that the one who appeared to the medium was the spirit of Samuel and not a demon calling itself by his name, as shown by the following:

28.9.2.en: 1- The alarm of the medium, who did not expect the spirit of Samuel himself to come.

28.9.3.en: 2- Samuel told Saul by a prophecy from God that he would die tomorrow, that the children of Israel would be defeated before the Philistines, and that David would become the king after him. And all this was fulfilled.

28.9.4.en: 3- Samuel's saying to Saul, "Why hast thou disquieted me," because the spirits of the righteous are with God and are not occupied with anything else.

28.9.5.en: 4- The testimony of the medium that she saw gods ascending, that is, a powerful spirit different from what she was accustomed to see of the spirits of demons.

28.9.6.en: 5- The testimony of the Holy Bible itself to this in the Book of Jesus ben Sirach: "And after his death he prophesied, and showed the king his end" ... (Sir 46:23).

28.10.0.en: Saul wanted to reassure the woman again, so he said to her, "Be not afraid," and asked her what she had seen. She answered him that she had seen something great and new to her, namely gods ascending out of the earth. By the word "gods" it is meant that she may have seen the spirits of saints or angels who accompanied Samuel in his appearing, or perhaps it was Samuel alone, but from the splendor of his form she used the expression "gods" in the plural, which is the expression used by all the pagan sorcerers of that time.

28.11.0.en: Saul asked her more closely what his form was, and she told him that he was an old man, that is, advanced in age and days, covered with a mantle. This was in fact Samuel's clothing during his ministry on earth, and so Saul was afraid and expressed his trembling by bowing to the ground.

28.12.0.en: The spirit of Samuel spoke, rebuking Saul for what he had done by his urgent desire to call up his spirit, which was rejoicing in praise before God and resting in peace, awaiting Christ's redemption to transfer it to Paradise. The First Book of Samuel. The expression "bringing me up" does not mean that Saul had authority to bring up his spirit, nor did the sorceress, because no one has authority over the world of spirits except God alone; rather it is a rebuke from Samuel's spirit to Saul for seeking to speak with spirits.

28.12.1.en: Saul answered Samuel that he had resorted to this when the Lord had closed all the ways before him and did not answer him by a prophet or a dream, and Samuel had been the last to speak to him with the voice of God. For this reason he sought his spirit so that he might tell him what to do in his war with the Philistines.

28.13.0.en: Samuel answered him with hard words: how dared Saul ask, when the Lord had departed from him completely? If God had wanted to speak with Saul and inform him of the matter, He would have used one of the other usual means, and not this way by which Saul transgressed the Law, so that he became a complete enemy of God.

28.14.0.en: The kingdom torn out of your hand: after Saul's death David will take a part of the kingdom, the tribe of Judah, and reign in Hebron, and Ish-bosheth the son of Saul will reign over the rest of the tribes; then Ish-bosheth will die and the whole kingdom will submit to David.

28.14.1.en: Samuel spoke in the past tense to confirm that the divine plan and God's absolute judgment had already gone forth from Him, to take the kingdom from Saul and give it to David the son of Jesse. The word "neighbour" does not mean physical kinship, but is because David was formerly close to Saul's table.

28.15.0.en: And all this has come upon you, and God has rejected you, because of your disobedience and your not obeying Him when He commanded you to kill "Agag," king of Amalek, and to destroy all that you took in the war, but you spared Agag and also much of his livestock.

28.16.0.en: Tomorrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: that is, in Hades, but the righteous in one place and the wicked in another.

28.16.1.en: And because of your other evils also, God will deliver you tomorrow, and with you the people of Israel, into the hand of the Philistines, and God will carry out His just judgment, so that you die with your sons and your spirits come to dwell with me. Likewise your army will lose the battle and be humiliated and given up to the Philistines.

28.16.2.en: Note: before Christ's redemption of mankind, the waiting place of departed spirits was one place, for the righteous, like Samuel the prophet, and also for the wicked, like Saul. But the righteous were in a better state, since they were awaiting the hope of Christ's redemption of them, while the wicked were in a very bad state, since they knew what their final fate was. And after Christ's redemption of mankind on the holy wood of the Cross, the Paradise of delight was opened and the righteous came to be in a place separate from the place of the wicked, which is the heavenly Paradise, while the wicked remained in Hades.

28.16.3.en: God's judgment and justice must be fulfilled, so do not persist in sin or justify it, but hasten to repentance and you will enjoy God's forgiveness and mercies, for He desires that all be saved. So draw near to Him, whatever your sins may be, for He is a loving Father.

28.17.0.en: Saul was terrified and completely broke down at the horror of what he heard, and he fell full length on the earth, for he would lose his life, his sons would die also, and he would lose the war. His muscles' slackening also helped to bring about his fall. The First Book of Samuel. And he felt weak, since he had eaten nothing all day. But sadly he did not think of offering repentance and returning to God.

28.18.0.en: When the woman, the medium, saw Saul's collapse, his weakness and his great fear, she said to him: I have listened to you and obeyed you, and I was at your command, and I put myself in danger and carried out all your orders; so now you also listen to my request, that I set a little food before you, so that you may eat and regain your strength, so that you can return and go back to your place in the midst of your army.

28.19.0.en: Saul refused to eat because of his great grief, but after the urging of the woman, the medium, and his two servants who had accompanied him to her, he listened to them and rose from the ground and sat on the woman's bed, while she killed her calf and baked flour into unleavened bread in order to honor the king. And indeed Saul ate with his two servants, and then they all departed to the camp of Israel to await the war the next day.

28.19.1.en: "Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap," so the Lord Christ has warned us, and how much harsher and more bitter was what Saul reaped from what he had sown before. So be careful and do not wrong anyone, and obey God and His commandments, and you will have deliverance and enjoy God's mercies in place of His justice and punishment. And accustom yourself to repentance from now on, because if you do not accustom yourself to it and then meet hard circumstances like Saul, you may not be able to, for lack of habit.

28.19.2.en: The Philistines prepare for war and David is excluded from taking part in it

29.0.0.en: Aphek: a place south of Shunem (ch. 28:4). After the Philistines first gathered at "Shunem," they began to move south to be nearer to the armies of the Israelites, and they assembled at the town of "Aphek" to organize their army before the war. Meanwhile the Israelites were stationed in Jezreel by a fountain, probably Harod, and it is most likely the spring of Jalud, which lies southeast of Jezreel.

29.1.0.en: Lords: chiefs and leaders or kings.

29.1.1.en: Rereward: the rear of the army.

29.1.2.en: The five kings of the Philistines advanced with their armies and led hundreds and thousands of men to war, and David too was compelled to go out with them, as King Achish had asked of him. Of course David did not know what to do: if he withdrew, his earlier deception of Achish would be exposed, and if he really entered the war he would be a traitor to God and to his people, which David would never do!!! But he prayed and waited for God to intervene to save him from this predicament.

29.2.0.en: The kings of the Philistines were five in number, one of them Achish, who had received David into his ranks and allowed him to dwell there, and who now also called him to fight with the ranks of his men. When the rest of the kings of the Philistines saw this, they objected to Achish about David's going out with them in this war. So Achish hastened to defend him, saying that he had been one of Saul's servants but had fled with his men to him, and he had received him and found nothing evil in him throughout his stay with them in the city of Ziklag.

29.3.0.en: The four kings of the Philistines objected to "Achish's" defense, and they were indeed wiser and more realistic. They explained in their objection that David would turn against them in the war in an attempt to appease Saul again, and would present their heads to him as a gift. For how could David betray his people, when he was a national and popular hero whom the women had earlier sung of after his victory over Goliath? And they suggested to Achish that he require him to stay in Ziklag and not leave it, and that he have no part at all in this war.

29.3.1.en: Do not be troubled when embarrassing situations meet you, however hard they may be, but lift up your heart to God and ask the intercession of the saints, and trust that God will not leave you but will deliver you and guide you and protect you, so that no harm will befall you.

29.4.0.en: Achish was compelled to yield to the opinion of the four kings, so he summoned David, and when he came, he began his speech to him in a tone of apology. He first praised him for his uprightness throughout the period of his stay in the land of the Philistines and said that he had found no evil in him, and he had wanted to take him with him to the war, but his opinion did not find acceptance with the chiefs of the Philistines. Therefore David must go back and return to his place at Ziklag and not take part in the war. Of course we see here how it was God's hand and providence that relieved David of the embarrassment and rescued him from the difficult situation, and God also brought him back to Ziklag, which the Amalekites had attacked, to save his household and his wives from this attack (ch. 30:

29.5.0.en: David hid his true feelings by God's mighty working, and how the apology had come from the Philistines, and he seized the opportunity and showed feigned emotion that he would not take part in the battle with Achish, and how could he remain far from the battle and not fight the Israelites.

29.6.0.en: Achish repeated his kind words to David and described him as being like a guardian angel from the gods to him, and made clear to him again that the rejection had not come from him but from the rest of the kings of the Philistines.

29.7.0.en: He also asked him to rise early in the morning with his men and return to "Ziklag," and indeed David did so and went back with his men to the lands of the Philistines and did not take part in the war, while the Philistines prepared to fight in Jezreel.

29.7.1.en: In the words of Achish, king of Gath, to the lords of the Philistines and to David, we see what shows his being moved and his great love for David, as appears in the following:

29.7.2.en: 1- His oath by the Lord in his saying, "As the Lord liveth" (v. 6), the original of which is "Yahweh," and this means Achish was influenced by David and took this oath from him.

29.7.3.en: 2- His testimony about David before the lords of the Philistines that he is upright (v. 6).

29.7.4.en: 3- His likening David to an angel in his speech with him (v. 9).

29.7.5.en: Because of the uprightness of David's heart, his enemies loved him and saw no fault in him. So be upright before God, and He will make all those around you live at peace with you, so that you can deal with them in peace and prosper in all your ways.

29.7.6.en: David pursues the Amalekites and defeats them
